announcements.text: Boeing Defense, Space & Security, a division of The Boeing Co., Seattle, Washington, has been awarded a $2,819,046,560 modification to a previously awarded contract (FA8625-11-C-6600) for 15 KC-46A Lot 13 production aircraft, G081, subscriptions, and licenses. Work will be performed in Seattle, Washington, and is expected to be completed by June 30, 2030. Fiscal 2027 aircraft procurement funds in the amount of $2,819,046,560 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity (For administrative purposes, this modification has been awarded under a new contract FA8609-27-C-B002).

announcements.text: Amentum Technology Inc., Tullahoma, Tennessee, has been awarded a cost-plus-fixed-fee $68,276,868 task order for the 21st Communication Squadron Bridge Contract support. This contract provides continuous 24/7/365 key mission communications, infrastructure sustainment, and secure information technology support services. Work will be performed at Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station, Colorado; and Peterson Space Force Base, Colorado, and is expected to be completed Dec. 20, 2028. This contract was a sole-source acquisition. Fiscal 2027 operation and maintenance funds in the amount of $11,943,767 are being obligated at the time of award. Space Systems Command, Peterson SFB, Colorado, is the contracting activity. (FA8723-27-F-B002).

announcements.text: Huntington Ingalls Inc. Newport News, Virginia, was awarded an $87,238,674 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification to previously awarded contract (N00024-21-C-2104) for Research and Development of advanced submarine technologies for current and future submarine platforms. This contract modification includes options which, if all exercised, would bring the cumulative value of the contract change to $494,927,401. Work will be performed in Newport News, Virginia, and is expected to be completed by September 2027. Fiscal 2027 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $6,830,000 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. (Awarded Nov. 20, 2026).

announcements.text: General Dynamics, Bath Iron Works, Bath, Maine, is awarded a $64,632,713 cost-plus-award-fee modification to a previously awarded contract N00024-24-C-2313 to exercise options for DDG 51 Class Lead Yard Support (LYS). Work will be performed in Bath, and Brunswick, Maine (99%); and Washington, D.C. (1%), and is expected to be completed by November 2027. Fiscal 2022 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $26,579,743 (43.4%); fiscal 2024 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $19,537,398 (31.9%); fiscal 2020 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $7,670,897 (12.6%); fiscal 2016 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $3,443,258 (5.6%); fiscal 2017 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $2,901,486 (4.8%); and fiscal 2019 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $1,053,552 (1.7%), will be obligated at time of award and funds in the amount of $3,443,258 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was not competitively procured in accordance with 10 U.S. Code 3204(a)(1) (only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements). Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity. (N00024-24-C-2313).

announcements.text: General Dynamics NASSCO-Norfolk, Norfolk, Virgina, is awarded a $20,971,962 cost-plus-award-fee contract for the accomplishment of Post Shakedown Availability (PSA) for USS Ted Stevens (DDG 128), with option for the accomplishment of PSA for USS William Charette (DDG 130). This contract includes options which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of this contract to $43,443,301. Work will be performed in Norfolk, Virgina (100%), and is expected to be completed by September 2027. If all options are exercised, work will continue through March 2030. Fiscal 2026 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $19,665,088 (100%) will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via sam.gov website, with three offers received. PAE Maritime, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N61177-26-C-2307).

announcements.text: Defense Maritime Solutions Inc., Chesapeake, Virginia, is awarded a $13,589,620 modification to a previously awarded firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract (N55236-23-D-0002). This modification exercises Option Year Four for original equipment manufacturer support of waterjets, shafts, and seals for the Independence-variant Littoral Combat Ship class. The overall total contract value ceiling remains unchanged at $60,582,873. Work will be performed at Mayport, Florida (40%); San Diego, California (40%); and various locations determined at the delivery order level (20%), and is expected to be completed by December 2027. No funds will be obligated at the time of award of contract modification; funds will be obligated on individual delivery orders as they are issued. Southwest Regional Maintenance Center, San Diego, California, is the contracting activity.

announcements.text: Science Application International Corp., Reston, Virginia (HTC71123DD001), was awarded a $48,868,648 modification to increase the ordering ceiling of a previously awarded contract for Managed Information Technology Services. This contract modification is indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity with firm-fixed-price, labor hour, and time-and-material line items. This modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to an estimated $199,485,057. The modification provides continued strategic, technical, and program management guidance and support services to facilitate the operations and modernization of the combatant command’s infrastructure, systems, and applications. Work will be performed at the U.S. Transportation Command’s Office (USTRANSCOM), Washington, D.C.; the Pentagon, Washington, D.C.; the Joint Enabling Capabilities Command, Norfolk, Virginia; and Tampa, Florida. The ordering period should be Dec. 1, 2022, to Nov. 30, 2027. Transportation working capital funds and operations and maintenance funds are being used. The USTRANSCOM Directorate of Acquisition, Scott Air Force Base, Illinois, is the contracting activity.
